causal_graphs.context: K-12 tatD in pET22b expressed in BL21-CodonPlus-RIPL and purified by Ni-NTA and Q-Sepharose. Figure 2B uses 40 nM 5'-32P-labeled 20-nt ssDNA, 0-0.5 uM TatD, 2 mM Mg2+, 3 mM MOPS, 75 mM NaCl, pH 7.2, 10 uL, 37 C for 1 h. Substrate sequence is CAAACTCTCTCTCTCTCAAC.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2B is the adopted WT magnesium-dependent digestion experiment; 2C/D support direction. The cache records the exact Figure 2B assay, concentration series and metal controls.
Establishes native TatD family membership, not isolated-domain sufficiency or experimental clone sequencing.

edges.mechanism: The enzyme concentration series in the magnesium-containing reaction converts the 20-nt substrate into shorter gel-resolved products. Separate 5'- versus 3'-labeling and terminal-blocking tests support 3'-5' exonucleolysis without resolving the chemical microsteps.
edges.subject: tatd-magnesium-ssdna-system

causal_graphs.family_mapping: UniProtKB:P27859, tatD/b4483/JW5931, K-12 reference of 260 residues, sequence version 3; exact UniProt/InterPro sequence agreement and PF01026 at 2-257 inclusive. Native reference, DNA donor and expression host are distinct; the complete tagged clone sequence is not independently reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: This is a joint enzyme/substrate/cofactor assay, not magnesium sufficiency or all-family activity. No-metal, Ca2+ and Zn2+ negatives apply only to the tested ssDNA conditions; they do not exclude AP endonuclease activity on another substrate. Proposed metal stoichiometry and catalytic microsteps remain unresolved. The source's 20 mM protease-K quench unit is questionable and not silently corrected.

nodes.label: Tagged TatD plus 20-nt ssDNA and 2 mM Mg2+
Shorter labeled DNA products from the 20-nt substrate

causal_graphs.scope: Full-length E. coli TatD with a C-terminal His tag, not an isolated Pfam domain or a cellular repair pathway.
causal_graphs.title: Purified tagged TatD digests ssDNA in a magnesium-containing reaction

causal_graphs.context: WT and QuikChange mutants use the same purification workflow and 20-nt ssDNA assay. Figure 5C displays a 0.5/1/2 concentration series without units in its image or caption. General methods specify 37 C in MOPS/NaCl pH 7.2, but this panel's duration, DNA dose and metal concentration are not resolved; Figure 2B values are not substituted.

evidence.explanation: Figure 5C upper panel and active-site Results distinguish H62A from WT and the three other histidine substitutions; exact concentration units remain unresolved.

edges.mechanism: H62A shows substantially reduced digestion relative to WT in the same upper-panel concentration series, while H64A, H127A and H152A retain digestion. This establishes a substitution effect, not its unique chemical explanation.
edges.subject: h62a-substitution

evidence.explanation: Figure 5C lower panel directly compares E91A and WT; acidic-mutant Results qualify the caption's loss language as little residual activity, not an absolute zero-rate determination.

edges.mechanism: E91A leaves little residual digestion compared with the lower-panel WT series. The effect does not independently identify how many metal ions bind or distinguish catalytic from structural disruption.
edges.subject: e91a-substitution

evidence.explanation: Figure 5C lower panel and its Results support the E201A decrease; mutant purification is described but folding and exact panel doses are not independently resolved.

edges.mechanism: E201A leaves little residual digestion compared with the matched WT concentration series, without establishing a specific metal-coordination mechanism.
edges.subject: e201a-substitution

evidence.explanation: Figure 5C lower panel and active-site Results support the D203A decrease. Metal positions in structural superpositions remain proposals rather than observed causal edges.

edges.mechanism: D203A leaves little residual digestion compared with the lower-panel WT preparation. A direct effect on the measured reaction is retained without asserting a resolved catalytic-water pathway.
edges.subject: d203a-substitution

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P27859 sequence version 3 contains H62, E91, E201 and D203, all within PF01026 residues 2-257. H64, H127 and H152 are also verified and their alanine mutants retain activity. These are intact-protein perturbations, not isolated-domain tests.
causal_graphs.limitations: Directness refers to the measured biochemical digestion endpoint, not a demonstrated histidine general base, exact metal ligation or proton transfer. Altered folding or effective protein concentration is not excluded for every variant. Panel-specific dose units and complete clone sequences require follow-up.

nodes.label: Digestion of 20-nt ssDNA relative to the WT preparation

causal_graphs.scope: Separate purified single-residue variants of the full-length C-terminally tagged E. coli TatD preparation in Figure 5C.
causal_graphs.title: TatD H62A and acidic substitutions reduce ssDNA digestion

causal_graphs.context: Synthetic tatD in modified pET-21 produces untagged protein in BL21(DE3). Reaction contains 10 uM protein, 100 nM FAM-labeled THF duplex, 5 mM CaCl2, 20 mM EPPS pH 8.0, 50 mM NaCl and 2.5% glycerol at 37 C; gel time points are 1, 30 and 120 min. Table S1 gives FAM-CGTCTCCTGAAC/(THF)/GTGCTATCGCTC annealed with GAGCGATAGCACAGTTCAGGAGACG.

evidence.explanation: Published Figure 6 bacterial Results and nuclease Methods, checked against the visually inspected author-manuscript gel and Table S1, support this THF-duplex incision endpoint. Human and other bacterial paralog experiments are separate contexts.
evidence.snippet: robust AP endo activity on dsDNA

edges.mechanism: The TatD THF-duplex time course accumulates the discrete product assigned to AP-site-analogue incision. The complete preparation and reaction are the observed cause; the graph does not promote structural catalytic proposals or untested natural-AP activity to direct observations.
edges.subject: tatd-calcium-thf-duplex-system

causal_graphs.family_mapping: E. coli TatD reference P27859 maps to PF01026 residues 2-257. The synthetic gene's exact sequence/version and full clone junctions are not independently supplied here; current native mapping is not a tag or strain assertion about all bacterial paralogs.
causal_graphs.limitations: The measured substrate contains THF, not a natural AP site. No matched no-enzyme/mock-purification control is labeled for the bacterial Figure 6 lanes; human BH110 controls are not transferred. Substrate and metal both differ between Mg/exonuclease and Ca/AP panels, so calcium alone is not shown to switch activity. Table S1 places THF after 12 bases while the manuscript Figure 5 caption says position 12. No cellular repair chain or metal microstep is asserted.

nodes.label: Untagged TatD preparation plus THF duplex and 5 mM CaCl2
Discrete shorter labeled product from the internal-THF duplex

causal_graphs.scope: Purified E. coli TatD in the 2023 bacterial Figure 6 assay, not the human TATDN proteins or the 2014 tagged preparation.
causal_graphs.title: Untagged TatD preparation incises an internal AP-site analogue in duplex DNA

causal_graphs.context: Serial dilution spots with chronic 1 mM H2O2, incubated overnight at 37 C in Figure 3B. Drug-free spots are the unstressed comparator; separate MMS, MMC and UV-C tests do not display the same defect. Basal plate-medium details and exact deletion stock identity remain unresolved.

evidence.explanation: Figure 3B and cell-survival Methods establish the scoped chronic-peroxide phenotype. Drug-free and alternative-stressor comparisons limit generalization; no genetic rescue is shown for the adopted endpoint.

edges.mechanism: DeltaTatD spots grow less well than WT during chronic peroxide exposure. Whole-gene dependence is retained while the molecular cause of the growth defect remains unresolved.
edges.subject: tatd-deletion-under-peroxide

causal_graphs.family_mapping: K-12 tatD reference P27859/b4483/JW5931 contains PF01026 at 2-257, within 260 residues. Deleting the gene perturbs the whole protein; the tested stock's deletion boundaries are not independently reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: No genetic rescue is shown for this adopted comparison. Spot growth is not a quantified survival probability, and impaired peroxide growth does not establish a direct nuclease-to-repair-to-survival chain. Acute outgrowth and the later three-paralog deletion are different experiments.

nodes.label: DeltaTatD compared with WT during chronic 1 mM H2O2 exposure
Colony growth in the peroxide serial-spot assay

causal_graphs.scope: E. coli K-12 WT and DeltaTatD cells from the Keio collection; a whole-gene growth phenotype, not direct proof of a particular DNA-repair reaction.
causal_graphs.title: Whole-gene TatD deletion reduces colony growth under chronic peroxide

evidence.explanation: Main methods and Figures 2/3/5 support the adopted effects but leave mutant-panel doses, clone details, quench units and molecular microsteps unresolved.

Bacterial Figure 6 supports internal-THF incision; Table S1 and the manuscript caption disagree on site numbering. Human proteins, YcfH/YjjV and triple-knockout contexts need separately mapped curation.
